- If sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If sentiment is positive (avg > 0.2) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above recent high or use moving average smoothing.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3 in 3–5 days), model fails to capture momentum; add 0.5–1.0% lagged sentiment weight to next forecast.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices) but sentiment is weak, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period price (last 7–10 days) — cap forecast at 1–2% below true outcome’s final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history includes multiple +0.7 spikes, model tends to overreact; apply decay factor (e.g., 0.85) to sentiment influence in next 5 days.
